title: improv·artist · luminous (James Turrell)
mutation_directive: improv artist: luminous via James Turrell

improv_extras.practice: perception of light itself; rooms where the air seems solid

v1.feedback: The superellipse aperture frame is a legit Turrell reference — the rounded-rectangle void reads immediately as a Ganzfeld opening, and the indigo→rose→warm-white palette is restrained and appropriate. The inner glow plane selling 'solid light' through the aperture is a smart touch. Two things to push: the breathing/drift animation is too uniform — Turrell's power is that the light feels *still* yet your perception shifts, so dampen the sinusoidal motion significantly (halve amplitude, quarter frequency) and let the color cycle do the perceptual work instead. Second, the particle density falls off too gently at the outer edge, making the frame dissolve into the background rather than presenting a crisp architectural boundary — tighten the outer falloff in the luminosity curve so the aperture shape has a harder silhouette against the void.

v2.feedback: The superellipse aperture-within-frame is a legible Turrell Ganzfeld reference — form reads in under 2s and the rose/warm-white/pale-gold palette is restrained and appropriate. The inner glow particles could use a stronger radial density falloff and slightly higher luminance at center to sell the 'solid light' volumetric illusion; right now the aperture reads more as a flat tinted rectangle than air that glows. The frame surround is too uniform — Turrell's rooms have subtle gradient falloff toward the walls; adding a vignette or distance-based density taper on the frame particles would deepen the spatial read. The barely-perceptible drift is the right call for Turrell stillness, but the color cycle period could be even slower (0.012 instead of 0.025) to better match the glacial perceptual shifts of an actual Ganzfeld.
